clue.text: Elevate one among many

indicators.note: among says the word for one sits within the word for many

parts.note: a host is a great number, a multitude
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Lifting up one person from a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist something is to raise or lift it, as with a flag or sail.

clue.text: Furious because someone stepped on your toe?

definitions.text: Furious because someone stepped on your toe?

parts.words: Furious because someone stepped on your toe?
parts.note: the pain makes you jump about on one foot while being very angry

explanation.surface: Rage at someone treading on your foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means extremely angry, literally pictured as leaping about in pain.

clue.text: At the pub the posh finish with a round suggestion

parts.note: an inn is a pub
U is the abbreviation for upper-class
end means finish
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Upper-class drinkers ending the evening by proposing another round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a round of drinks; it is the circular letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: An innuendo is an indirect hint or insinuation.

clue.text: Roll rear of plane to fly

parts.note: to roll over is to turn
the tail is the back of an aircraft

explanation.surface: A pilot making an aircraft rotate during a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' is not about aircraft but means flee.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn tail is to run away, to flee.

clue.text: Out of town — and out of the country

explanation.surface: Somewhere neither urban nor rural, described twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: A suburb lies outside the town centre, yet it is not countryside either, so both readings fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Outskirts districts sit beyond the city proper; they are also distinct from rural land, so 'out of the country' in the sense of not rustic.

clue.text: Seven of them are all oceans

definitions.text: Seven of them are all oceans

parts.words: Seven of them are all oceans
parts.note: the phrase about the seven bodies covering the globe

explanation.surface: Claiming the world's waters number seven.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional seven seas stand for all the world's oceans.

clue.text: Falsely disloyal

parts.note: both wrong in fact and unfaithful to a partner

explanation.surface: Treacherous under false pretences.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both false, not accurate, and unfaithful.

clue.text: Rift created by a broken promise?

explanation.surface: A split caused by failing to keep one's word.
explanation.walkthrough: Breach of promise was a legal action for breaking an engagement to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach is a gap or rupture; it is also the breaking of an agreement or promise.

clue.text: It may be held in revulsion

definitions.text: It may be held in revulsion

parts.words: It may be held in revulsion
parts.note: facing a foul smell, people pinch this facial feature shut

explanation.surface: Something gripped in disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: People hold their nose to block a disgusting smell.

clue.text: Review troops in central America

indicators.note: in places the troops inside the Central American country

parts.note: Panama is a country in Central America
OR, other ranks, is the usual abbreviation for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Inspecting soldiers somewhere in Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central America' is not a geographical picker taking middle letters; it points to a country there.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a broad survey or overview of a subject, much like a general review.

clue.text: Capone's nickname comes from unusual fracas with church

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of fracas come out in an odd new order

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: A gangster's nickname supposedly stems from a strange brawl in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges FRACAS to SCARFA, then CE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Capone, the Chicago mobster, was known by this name because of facial scars.

clue.text: Whip — it's raised in hunting

indicators.note: in places the reversed letters within the hunting word

parts.note: a chase is a hunt

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means read upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: A hunting crop lifted during the hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns ITS into STI, set inside CHASE.
explanation.definitionFit: To chastise is to punish, originally by beating.

clue.text: I earn it from a sort of selling

indicators.note: from signals the answer is made out of the letters of I earn it, reworked

explanation.surface: Someone boasting of earning money by a particular sales method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' rearranges the letters of 'I earn it'. Inertia selling means sending goods unasked and billing unless they are returned.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia selling is a named sales technique relying on the buyer's failure to act.

clue.text: Urge pa, go around with people of the same generation

indicators.note: around tells us the letters of urge pa go are moved about

explanation.surface: Encouraging father to travel with his peers.
explanation.definitionFit: An age group is a set of people born at about the same time.

clue.text: Fruit stolen — used as missiles?

parts.note: grapes are a fruit
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: Stolen fruit being thrown as missiles.
explanation.definitionFit: Grapeshot was a cluster of small iron balls fired from a cannon as projectiles.

clue.text: Moving-picture?

parts.note: a film that moves its audience emotionally, rather than a motion picture

explanation.surface: Just a film.
explanation.definitionFit: A weepie is a sentimental film designed to make viewers cry.

clue.text: Noted example of inspired lunacy?

parts.note: a famous piece of music, noted in the sense of written in notes, inspired by the moon, lunar lunacy

explanation.surface: A celebrated case of brilliant madness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lunacy' comes from Latin luna, the moon; 'noted' hints at written music, here Beethoven's piano work.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Piano Sonata No 14 got its popular title from a critic likening it to moonlit water.

clue.text: Put out, away, and finished

parts.note: off means away
ended means finished

explanation.surface: Ejected, sent off, and done for.
explanation.definitionFit: To be put out is to be upset or affronted.

clue.text: A place of grazing

parts.note: a scraped patch of skin rather than a field where animals feed

explanation.surface: A field where livestock feed.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrasion is a scraped area of skin, a graze.

clue.text: They may strengthen or weaken an army

definitions.text: They may strengthen or weaken an army

parts.words: They may strengthen or weaken an army
parts.note: military units add strength, while splits and disagreements weaken a force

explanation.surface: Things that can make or break a fighting force.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both large military formations and rifts or disagreements.

clue.text: Horrid sailor admitted? It's not impossible

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the sailor goes inside

parts.note: vile means horrid
AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A nasty seaman has been let in, which could happen.
explanation.definitionFit: Viable means workable or feasible.

clue.text: Songbird with little relation to others

parts.note: sis is short for sister
kin are one's related others, family

explanation.surface: A bird barely connected to its fellows.
explanation.definitionFit: A siskin is a small finch.

clue.text: Cheer for most of the players at end of game

indicators.note: most of says the word for the players loses its final letter

parts.note: a cricket or football side is an eleven

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of game

explanation.surface: Applause for nearly all the team when the match ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate someone is to raise their spirits, to buoy or uplift them.

clue.text: Wing patterns have changed

indicators.note: have changed tells us the letters of patterns are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bird plumage markings have altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wing' suggests a bird; it is the arm of a cross-shaped church.
explanation.definitionFit: A transept is either arm of a cruciform church, crossing the nave like a wing.

clue.text: Bite from upset insect

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a gnat is a small insect

explanation.surface: A bite from an irritated bug.
explanation.definitionFit: Tang is a sharp, biting flavour.

clue.text: The first embrace for the ruffian

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word the

parts.note: a hug is an embrace

explanation.surface: The thug's first hug.
explanation.definitionFit: A thug is a violent criminal or bully.

clue.text: Robin to indicate complicity in trick

parts.note: Robin Hood, the legendary outlaw
a wink signals a shared secret

explanation.surface: An outlaw signals he is in on the con.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoodwink is to deceive or fool someone.

clue.text: Fag-end got bent in picking up the pieces

indicators.note: end picks the final letter of the word fag

parts.note: leaning means inclined or bent over

explanation.surface: A cigarette butt crumpled while someone tidies up the mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fag' is British slang for a cigarette, so 'fag-end' looks like a butt, but only its last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Gleaning is collecting leftover grain after harvest, gathering scraps.

clue.text: He gave the rondo new form

indicators.note: new form says the letters of rondo are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A composer reworked a piece of music in rondo form.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor is someone who gives, such as blood or money.
